newsitem.title: USA: Norfolk Southern sees new legal action.
newsitem.headline: Norfolk Southern sees new legal action.

text.p: An attorney for Norfolk Southern Corp said it would be "safe to assume" the railroad would take new legal action in the near future in response to an increased bid by CSX Corp for Conrail Inc.

The attorney, Steven Rothschild, declined to specify what action Norfolk Southern would take, but he said an new extension of the exclusivity period in the CSX-Conrail merger agreement was "outrageous" and legally vulnerable.
"It is probably safe to assume that there will be actions taken by us," Rothschild said.
Norfolk Southern had unsucessfully challenged in court an earlier agreement by Conrail in its proposed merger with CSX not to consider any third-party offer until July 1997.
U.S. District Judge Donald Van Artsdalen, in denying last month a Norfolk Southern request for an emergency injunction to block the merger, said Conrail had a right to agree to an exclusivity period.

"(T)he directors have every right to favor one competing bid over another...And certainly it seems to me that it (Conrail) can agree not to shop their (CSX's) proposal after signing a merger agreement," Van Artsdalen said.
